# nish/net/http-compress

content coding for HTTP responses (RFC 9110 §8.4 and §12.5.3): reading a request's `Accept-Encoding` and compressing a body with `Content-Encoding: gzip`, for any of the three servers.

```ts
import {
  HTTP1_GZIP_FIELD_BYTES,
  HTTP_CODING_DEFLATE,
  HTTP_CODING_GZIP,
  HTTP_CODING_IDENTITY,
  HTTP_CODING_NONE,
  HTTP_COMPRESS_NOT_ACCEPTED,
  HTTP_COMPRESS_NO_FEWER_SEGMENTS,
  HTTP_COMPRESS_SENT,
  HTTP_COMPRESS_TOO_LARGE,
  HTTP_COMPRESS_TOO_LITTLE_SAVED,
  HTTP_COMPRESS_TOO_SMALL,
  HTTP_DEFAULT_MSS,
  HTTP_ENCODER_AUTO,
  HTTP_ENCODER_FIXED,
  HTTP_ENCODER_LEVEL,
  HTTP_OFFER_DEFLATE,
  HTTP_OFFER_GZIP,
  HttpCompressor,
  httpAcceptEncoding,
  httpCompressorDefault,
  httpIdentityRefused,
  httpSegments,
} from "nish/net/http-compress";
```

```ts
import { DEFLATE_FAST } from "nish/compress/deflate";
import { HTTP_CODING_GZIP, HttpCompressor } from "nish/net/http-compress";

const enc = new HttpCompressor(DEFLATE_FAST, 1024, 65536); // once per thread
// HTTP/1.1, in one call:
conn.respondEncoded(200, names, values, body, 0, n, enc, conn.acceptEncoding());
// HTTP/2 or HTTP/3, by hand:
const coding: i32 = httpAcceptEncoding(value, 0, toI32(value.length), HTTP_OFFER_GZIP);
const m: i32 = enc.compress(coding, body, 0, n);
if (m >= 0) {
  enc.addFields(names, values);
  h2.respond(id, 200, enc.names, enc.values, false);
  h2.write(id, enc.output, 0, m);
}
```

The content coding to send for the `Accept-Encoding` field value `buf[start .. end)` among the codings `offered` (`HTTP_OFFER_GZIP | HTTP_OFFER_DEFLATE`): `HTTP_CODING_GZIP`, `HTTP_CODING_DEFLATE`, `HTTP_CODING_IDENTITY` or `HTTP_CODING_NONE`, by the rules in the module comment.

</scalar-card>

A compressor for the usual server: `DEFLATE_FAST`, bodies of 1 KB to 1 MB.

</scalar-card>

Whether the `Accept-Encoding` value in `buf[start .. end)` refuses the body as it is: `identity;q=0`, or `*;q=0` with no `identity` listed.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="httpSegments" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#httpsegments">

</scalar-card>

<scalar-detail title="Opt-in">

Nothing here runs unless the program asks: it decides which
responses to compress, and `HttpCompressor` declines any body shorter than
its `minLength`, longer than its `maxLength`, or that gzip would not make
smaller, answering -1 so the program sends the bytes as they are.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Compression that pays for itself">

A body is sent compressed only when
it saves at least `minSaving` bytes and `minSavingPercent` percent of the
body; otherwise the compressed bytes are dropped and the body goes as it
is. With `segmentMode` set, `respondEncoded` also sends it compressed only
when the whole response, head included, takes fewer TCP segments of `mss`
bytes (the connection's `mss` if set, else the compressor's, 1448 by
default): a 1300-byte body that gzips to 700 still fits in one segment
either way. After each call `decision` says why (`HTTP_COMPRESS_SENT`,
`_NOT_ACCEPTED`, `_TOO_SMALL`, `_TOO_LARGE`, `_TOO_LITTLE_SAVED`,
`_NO_FEWER_SEGMENTS`), for a program to count. A response whose identity
form already fits one segment is `_NO_FEWER_SEGMENTS` without running gzip
at all, as no compression could take fewer.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Two encoders">

Bodies up to `fixedLimit` (16 KB) go through
`GzipFixedCompressor`: one fixed-Huffman block, a 16 KB window, no state
between calls, two to four times faster than `DEFLATE_FAST` on 0.5 to
16 KB of JSON for output about 1.35 times larger. Larger bodies go through
the `GzipCompressor` at the level given; `encoder` forces either one.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Vary: Accept-Encoding">

**`Vary: Accept-Encoding`** (with `vary`, on by default) goes on every
response whose coding depended on the request: one sent compressed, and
one sent as it is because the request did not accept gzip. A body that is
too small, too large or did not pay is sent the same to every client, so
it carries no `Vary`. A request that refuses identity (`identity;q=0`)
and accepts gzip is sent gzip whatever the policy (`compressAnyway`).

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Negotiation">

**Negotiation** (`httpAcceptEncoding`) follows §12.5.3: each listed coding
with its q-value, `x-gzip` as `gzip`, `*` for every coding not listed, and
`identity` acceptable unless it is given q=0, directly or through `*`. Of
the codings the program offers, the most preferred with q above 0 wins, the
program's order (gzip, then deflate) breaking ties; it beats `identity` at
an equal q, and beats an `identity` the field does not mention at any q. With no field at all the answer is
`HTTP_CODING_IDENTITY` (the RFC allows any coding then, but a client that
says nothing is safest sent nothing it may not read); an empty field asks
for identity too. `HTTP_CODING_NONE` means nothing offered is acceptable
and identity is refused: a server may answer 406 or send identity anyway.
A malformed element is skipped. The parser allocates nothing.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Compressing allocates nothing">

**Compressing allocates nothing** and caches nothing between responses:
`HttpCompressor` holds a `GzipCompressor`, a `GzipFixedCompressor`, an
output buffer of `compressBound(maxLength)` bytes and
the field arrays `addFields` fills, all built once.
`HTTP_CODING_DEFLATE` (zlib framing) is negotiated but not produced: a
client that accepts only `deflate` is sent identity, which every client
reads.

</scalar-detail>

## httpAcceptEncoding

The content coding to send for the `Accept-Encoding` field value
`buf[start .. end)` among the codings `offered` (`HTTP_OFFER_GZIP |
HTTP_OFFER_DEFLATE`): `HTTP_CODING_GZIP`, `HTTP_CODING_DEFLATE`,
`HTTP_CODING_IDENTITY` or `HTTP_CODING_NONE`, by the rules in the module
comment. A window outside `buf` panics.

```ts
function httpAcceptEncoding(
  buf: u8[],
  start: i32,
  end: i32,
  offered: i32,
): i32
```

## httpIdentityRefused

Whether the `Accept-Encoding` value in `buf[start .. end)` refuses the
body as it is: `identity;q=0`, or `*;q=0` with no `identity` listed. A
server should then send a coding the client takes even where it would not
bother (`HttpCompressor.compressAnyway`).

```ts
function httpIdentityRefused(
  buf: u8[],
  start: i32,
  end: i32,
): boolean
```

## HttpCompressor

Compresses response bodies with gzip into a buffer of its own, and builds
the response fields that say so. One per thread; allocated once.

```ts
class HttpCompressor
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new HttpCompressor( level: i32, minLength: i32, maxLength: i32, )` | A compressor at `level` (`DEFLATE_FAST` suits a server) for bodies of `minLength` to `maxLength` bytes. A level outside 0 to 9, a negative `minLength` or a `maxLength` below it panics. |
| `readonly acceptEncodingValue: u8[]` |  |
| `readonly contentEncodingName: u8[]` |  |
| `decision: i32` | The last decision, an `HTTP_COMPRESS_*`; `HTTP_COMPRESS_NOT_ACCEPTED` before any. |
| `encoder: i32` | `HTTP_ENCODER_AUTO` (the default), `HTTP_ENCODER_FIXED` or `HTTP_ENCODER_LEVEL`. |
| `encoderRuns: i32` | How many times `compress` and `compressAnyway` ran an encoder, from 0: a count for a test or a profile to read, never consulted by a decision. It wraps past 2^31 - 1 to -2^31 rather than panic, as a server can run that many; read it as a difference between two reads. |
| `readonly fixed: GzipFixedCompressor` | The small-body encoder: one fixed-Huffman block, nothing kept between calls. |
| `fixedLimit: i32` | The longest body `HTTP_ENCODER_AUTO` gives the fixed-Huffman encoder: 16384 by default. |
| `readonly gzip: GzipCompressor` |  |
| `readonly gzipValue: u8[]` |  |
| `readonly maxLength: i32` |  |
| `readonly minLength: i32` | The shortest body worth compressing, and the longest the output can hold. |
| `minSaving: i32` | The least a compressed body must save to be sent: `minSaving` bytes and `minSavingPercent` percent of the body, whichever is more. 1 and 0 by default (any saving at all); a value below those counts as them. |
| `minSavingPercent: i32` |  |
| `mss: i32` |  |
| `readonly names: u8[][]` | The fields `addFields` built: the program's, then `Content-Encoding` and `Vary`. |
| `readonly output: u8[]` | Where `compress` writes; valid until the next call. |
| `segmentMode: boolean` | Whether `respondEncoded` also sends the compressed response only when, head included, it takes fewer TCP segments of `mss` bytes than the body as it is; off by default. `mss` is `HTTP_DEFAULT_MSS` unless the program sets it, or a connection's own `mss` overrides it. |
| `readonly values: u8[][]` |  |
| `vary: boolean` | Whether `addFields` adds `Vary: Accept-Encoding` (RFC 9110 §12.5.5), which a cache needs whenever the same resource may be sent either way. On by default; turn it off when the program sets its own `Vary`. |
| `readonly varyName: u8[]` |  |
| `addFields(names: u8[][], values: u8[][]): void` | Sets `names` / `values` to the program's fields followed by `Content-Encoding: gzip` and, when `vary`, `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. The arrays are reused, so after the first few calls this allocates nothing; they hold until the next call. |
| `addVary(): void` | Appends `Vary: Accept-Encoding` to the arrays `identityFields` built when `vary` is set and the last decision `varies`. |
| `compress( coding: i32, body: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, ): i32` | Compresses `body[off .. off + len)` into `output` when the length is in `[minLength, maxLength]`, `coding` is `HTTP_CODING_GZIP` and gzip saves what `minSaving` and `minSavingPercent` ask; answers the compressed length, or -1 to send the body as it is, and sets `decision` either way. `encoder` picks the encoder; the fixed-Huffman one stops as soon as its output passes what would be kept. A window outside `body` panics. |
| `compressAnyway( coding: i32, body: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, ): i32` | `compress` for a client that refuses identity (`httpIdentityRefused`): gzip whatever the body's length, the saving or the segments, so long as it is no longer than `maxLength`. Answers the compressed length, or -1 when `coding` is not gzip or the body is too long (sent as it is, which RFC 9110 §12.5.3 allows). |
| `fewerSegments( identityBytes: i32, encodedBytes: i32, mss: i32, ): boolean` | `segmentMode`'s rule, for a response of `identityBytes` bytes sent as it is or `encodedBytes` compressed, heads included, at `mss` bytes a segment (`this.mss` when 0 or less): whether the compressed one takes fewer segments. When it does not, `decision` becomes `HTTP_COMPRESS_NO_FEWER_SEGMENTS`. `respondEncoded` calls it; a program driving HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 by hand may with its own head sizes. |
| `http1IdentityHead( encodedHead: i32, encodedLength: i32, length: i32, ): i32` | The bytes of the HTTP/1.1 head a `length`-byte body sent as it is would get, from `encodedHead`, that of the same response sent compressed as `encodedLength` bytes with the fields `addFields` built: less `Content-Encoding: gzip`, less `Vary` (a body the segment count kept as it is would go out so to any client), and the other `Content-Length`. |
| `identityFields( names: u8[][], values: u8[][], ): void` | Sets `names` / `values` to the program's fields and, when `vary` and the last decision `varies`, `Vary: Accept-Encoding`: the fields of a body sent as it is from a resource that is sometimes compressed. |
| `leastSaving(len: i32): i32` | The bytes a compressed `len`-byte body must save: `minSaving` and `minSavingPercent`, at least 1. |
| `oneSegment( coding: i32, len: i32, mss: i32, ): boolean` | `segmentMode`'s shortcut, before any encoder runs: whether a `len`-byte body that `compress` would try (its length in `[minLength, maxLength]` and `coding` gzip) is no longer than one segment of `mss` bytes (as `fewerSegments` reads it). Sent as it is, such a response takes one segment once its head fits beside it, and no compression takes fewer, so `decision` becomes `HTTP_COMPRESS_NO_FEWER_SEGMENTS` and the caller checks the head: when it does not fit, the caller goes on to `compress`, which decides again. Anything else answers false and leaves `decision` alone. |
| `segmentSize(mss: i32): i32` | The segment `segmentMode` counts in: `mss` when above 0, else `this.mss` when above 0, else `HTTP_DEFAULT_MSS`. |
| `varies(): boolean` | Whether the last decision depended on the request's `Accept-Encoding`, so the response needs `Vary: Accept-Encoding`: a body sent compressed, or one sent as it is because the client did not take gzip. A body the lengths or the saving kept as it is would go out the same to any client. |

<scalar-card title="24" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP1_GZIP_FIELD_BYTES: i32`

The bytes `content-encoding: gzip` adds to an HTTP/1.1 head: name, value, ": " and CRLF.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP_CODING_DEFLATE: i32`

`deflate`: the zlib format (RFC 9110 §8.4.1.2).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP_CODING_GZIP: i32`

`gzip` (RFC 9110 §8.4.1.3), or its alias `x-gzip`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP_CODING_IDENTITY: i32`

No content coding: the body as it is.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP_CODING_NONE: i32`

Nothing offered is acceptable, identity included (§12.5.3: 406, or identity anyway).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP_COMPRESS_NOT_ACCEPTED: i32`

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP_COMPRESS_NO_FEWER_SEGMENTS: i32`

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP_COMPRESS_SENT: i32`

What `HttpCompressor.compress` (and `respondEncoded`'s segment check) last
decided, in `HttpCompressor.decision`, for a program to count: the body
went out compressed; the client did not take gzip; it was shorter than
`minLength`; longer than `maxLength`; gzip did not save `minSaving` bytes
and `minSavingPercent` percent; or the compressed response would not have
taken fewer TCP segments (`segmentMode`), which includes an identity
response that already fits one segment, decided without compressing.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP_COMPRESS_TOO_LARGE: i32`

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP_COMPRESS_TOO_LITTLE_SAVED: i32`

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP_COMPRESS_TOO_SMALL: i32`

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1,448" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP_DEFAULT_MSS: i32`

The maximum segment size `segmentMode` counts with unless told the
connection's: a 1500-byte Ethernet MTU less 20 bytes of IPv4 header, 20 of
TCP header and 12 of the timestamp option.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`HTTP_ENCODER_AUTO: i32`

`HttpCompressor.encoder`: by the body's length (the fixed-Huffman encoder up
to `fixedLimit` bytes, the constructor's level above), the fixed-Huffman
encoder always, or the constructor's level always.

</scalar-card>
